marisol.title: Margin Notes
marisol.text: Marisol shows Sam her father's old ledgers in the dusty back room, and her own corrections in the margins: years of tidy, furious red ink, her gold hoops catching the lamp. "He never listened. You actually do." It sounds like an accusation. It isn't. She taps the page with an ink-stained finger and won't look up.

choices.label: Ask her to walk you through one
choices.res: She walks him through a column from six years ago, and he listens to every number. At the end she closes the book gently, as if it had finally been read.

choices.label: Tell her the margins are the best part
choices.res: "The margins are the best part," Sam says. {N} stares at him, then scribbles something in a corner, grinning, and hides it.

image.comp: showing him old ledgers covered in her margin notes, leaning over a desk together
image.setting: owner's office, stacks of ledgers, lamplight

marisol.title: Invoice Ambush
marisol.text: Marisol barges into the washroom mid-argument about invoices, waving a handful of paper, sees Sam in the tub, and keeps arguing. Her gold hoops swing with every point, and her amber eyes fix on the ceiling at the third. She is competitive enough to not give ground even now, and Sam is too wet to take notes.

choices.label: Argue back from the tub
choices.res: He wins, for once. She claims it doesn't count, since he had the unfair advantage of being undressed, and stalks out with her chin high.

choices.label: Ask for some privacy
choices.res: She rolls her eyes, leaves the invoice on the stool, and shuts the door. Firmly. A moment later, through the wood: "Pay it by Friday."

choices.label: Splash her
choices.res: War is declared. The washroom floods, her skirt is soaked, and she retaliates with the sponge. Mira is not amused.

image.comp: standing in a washroom doorway waving an invoice, mid-argument, not leaving
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, a man in the tub off-frame

marisol.title: House Rules
marisol.text: Marisol beats Sam at cards four times in a row, snapping each hand down with relish, curls bouncing. Then she lets him win once, badly, with a deliberately terrible bluff. "I wanted to see your face," she says, and laughs until she can't breathe, gold hoops swinging, one hand pressed to her ribs.

choices.label: Demand a rematch, with stakes
choices.res: The stakes are a week of ledger duty. He loses again. She lets him pick the penalty, and it takes her a surprisingly long time to say no.

choices.label: Admit that his face was worth it
choices.res: "Worth every coin," Sam says. {N} wipes her eyes and, for once, doesn't reach for a witty retort, only another deck.

image.comp: slapping a winning hand of cards on the table, laughing at his face
image.setting: staff room at night, cards and coins on the table

marisol.title: A Letter
marisol.text: A letter arrives from Marisol's father, creased and salt-stained. He's alive, across the sea, and in debt again. She reads it three times at the ledger desk, jaw tight, and wants to sell something, anything, to bail him out. The ink on her fingers has begun to smear the page.

choices.label: "No. He left you with all of this."
choices.res: "He's not YOUR father." She slams the door, and the hoops on her ears chime. She apologizes the next day; so does he.

choices.label: Send him 300g
choices.res: She stares at the coins for a long time. "You didn't have to." "I know."

cantAfford.res: You can't spare it. She understands. Mostly.

choices.label: Help her write back
choices.res: It takes all night, three drafts and a pot of tea. The letter says no, kindly. She sleeps better than she has in years, her head on the ledger.

image.comp: reading a letter with a stricken expression, his hand on her shoulder

marisol.title: Her Mother
marisol.text: Marisol takes Sam to a small grave on the hill above town, wind combing the long grass, a single faded ribbon tied to the stone. Her mother's. She doesn't say much. The gold hoops are still, for once, and her hand is shoved deep in her pocket.

choices.label: Bring flowers
choices.res: She tells him three stories about her mother on the walk back, the lemon cake, the singing, the sums on the backs of invoices. She has never told anyone.

choices.label: Just stand with her
choices.res: After a while she leans against his shoulder, all her competitive edges gone soft, and they watch the clouds cross the stone together.

image.comp: standing at a small grave on a hill with him, holding wildflowers, quiet
image.setting: hilltop graveyard above a fantasy town, overcast

marisol.title: A New Deed
marisol.text: Marisol tears the old deed in half and writes a new one with both their names, her ink-stained fingers steady. The candle gutters in the ledger room where she grew up. "Partners," she says. "In every sense. Don't make me say it twice." Then she kisses him, gold hoops cold against his cheek, and says nothing else for a long while.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: {N} slides the new deed across the desk and taps the line left blank. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." Her pen stays ready.
